title: QQ Sparse Random Completion v1 implementation
objective: Compile arbitrary-width bounded and reciprocal-uniform 1/n dense QQ random_matrix generation directly into one owned FmpqMatrix resource call, preserving seeded and fallback semantics with competitive warm performance

handoff.summary: Dense QQ random_matrix now compiles arbitrary-width bounded values and Sage-compatible reciprocal-uniform 1/n values into one source-transparent native call. The kernel constructs, mutates, and returns its owned FmpqMatrix resource, publishes the exact next shared random word, and retains a same-semantics portable fallback. Native-disabled parity covers five seeds, one-word, 80/97-bit, 17/521-bit skew, integral, sparse 1/n, omitted-density 1/n, and collisions. The allocator-domain subprocess closes a matrix containing greater-than-64-bit entries twice. On linux-x64, 200x300 density=.2 warm medians were 2.95 ms for small bounds, 8.74 ms for 80/97-bit bounds, 9.34 ms for 17/521-bit skew, and 1.98 ms for 1/n, versus SageMath medians of 1.81, 4.56, 3.86, and 1.36 ms; the 1000x1000 density=.1 wide case was 76.48 ms with 130.5 MiB retained RSS growth.
risks: A host-addon-created FmpqMatrix borrowed by a separately statically linked native kernel was experimentally rejected: growing big fmpz entries in the kernel and destroying them in the host addon crossed FLINT/GMP allocator domains and segfaulted. Variable-size foreign resources must be constructed, mutated, and destroyed in one generated addon unless a shared-library allocator ABI is proved. The selected kernel-owned return pattern satisfies that invariant without compiler, FFI, or handwritten native changes.

One initial full native run stopped when an unrelated exact-polynomial timing ratchet measured 4.17x work for 2x input under concurrent builds. Its isolated immediate rerun passed, and a fresh recorded 663-second full native run passed every package, sanitizer, compiler, migration, matrix, and polynomial gate. This confirms host-load sensitivity in timing ratchets rather than a reproducible regression.
The retained benchmark is linux-x64 evidence. Windows x64, macOS arm64, and linux arm64 rely on the same-source fallback and declared FLINT resource machinery but still need platform CI evidence.

Each selected rational still calls declared fmpq_matrix_set_entry inside the isolated core. This has no host crossings and scales with selected entries, but future bulk FLINT APIs may reduce per-entry retained-byte accounting overhead further.
next_steps: Teach architecture guidance and, where feasible, compiler validation that variable-size foreign-resource allocation and destruction must share an allocator/provenance domain.
Run the retained benchmark and native lifecycle regression on macOS arm64, linux arm64, and Windows x64 before integration.

Integrate this lane after independent review, then reuse the kernel-owned construct/mutate/return pattern for other variable-size generated resources rather than adding operation-specific host adapters.
